name: Nujabes
discourse_profile: Nujabes began making tracks because he 'wanted to hear music that sampled the old soul and jazz I liked' — production as curation of a personal canon. His method centered on finding what his A&R Takeuchi called 'the best two bars' — isolating the emotional peak of a jazz or soul record and building outward from that loop, prioritizing the melodic arc of the source over rhythmic chopping. He rejected formula explicitly: 'Track makers often fail to see a lot of it. It's like they're conforming to a certain formula... they're unable to detach their music from those commercial aspects.' His Shibuya record shop Guinness stocked underground hip-hop and sample sources almost exclusively — Pase Rock recalls that 'Jun didn't really like the commercial hip-hop, so if it wasn't like DJ Premier, Pete Rock, or Five Deez, he wasn't with it.' Collaboration was face-to-face and non-negotiable: he flew MCs like Shing02, Substantial, and Cise Starr to Tokyo rather than exchanging files, sitting next to them during recording to direct flow and phrasing despite limited English — 'I don't want my music being used by randoms that don't understand my music.' He resisted the 'jazzy hip-hop' genre label — 'Isn't simply calling it hip-hop good?' — and by Modal Soul was pivoting from sample-based production toward live instrumentation with Uyama Hiroto, declaring 'I'm going to make my own orchestra.' Each song took at least a year from inception to release; Funky DL describes him as 'very selective in what would be released, even though he'd record a lot of songs.'
